plan.contextChunk: This figure pairs a coordinate diagram with a magnified inset to define the volume element in spherical coordinates. On the left, x, y, and z axes radiate from a common origin and a small curved orange box floats above the first octant, bounded by two dashed circular arcs of slightly different radii and by dashed rays fanning out from the origin. A bracket on the z axis marks the radial increment Delta rho, the angular gap between the two rays reaching the box is marked Delta phi, and a small angle in the horizontal plane near the origin is marked Delta theta. A flat blue quadrilateral in the xy-plane is the projection of the box, with a bracket beneath labeled rho sin phi and an arrow into it labeled rho sin phi Delta theta. A thick gray curved arrow sweeps right to an enlarged copy of the same box, whose three edges are labeled Delta rho, rho Delta phi, and rho sin phi Delta theta, with Delta V = rho^2 sin phi Delta rho Delta phi Delta theta printed below. Showing the subbox in place and again blown up lets each edge be matched to the coordinate increment that generates it. The construction motivates the factor rho^2 sin phi that appears when a triple integral is rewritten in spherical coordinates.

dashed circular arcs of radius ρ and ρ+Δρ in a vertical meridian plane, connecting the origin to the box
dashed rays fanning out from the origin bounding the Δφ angular gap
bracket on the z axis marking Δρ between the two sphere radii
Δφ angle arc near the origin between the two meridian rays
Δθ angle arc in the xy-plane near the origin

bracket beneath the projection labeled ρ sin φ, with an arrow labeled ρ sin φ Δθ
thick gray curved arrow sweeping from the coordinate diagram to the magnified inset
enlarged orange copy of the box (inset) with its three edges labeled Δρ, ρΔφ, and ρ sin φ Δθ
equation text ΔV = ρ² sin φ Δρ Δφ Δθ beneath the inset
highlighted matching-edge indicator shown simultaneously on the in-place box and the inset box

interactions.label: Δρ (radial increment)
interactions.teaches: Stretching the radial increment thickens the box between the two spheres — this edge's length is the raw increment Δρ itself, with no scaling factor

interactions.label: Δφ (polar angle increment)
interactions.teaches: Widening the polar angle gap stretches the box along the meridian arc — the edge length is the arc ρΔφ, which grows with distance ρ from the origin, not the raw angle

interactions.label: Δθ (azimuth increment)
interactions.teaches: Widening the azimuth gap stretches the box along the latitude circle — the edge length is ρ sin φ Δθ, shrinking toward the z axis, which is exactly where the sin φ factor in ΔV comes from

interactions.label: Edge labels
interactions.teaches: Matching each edge of the small in-place box to its blown-up labeled counterpart shows why two of the three edges are arc lengths (ρΔφ, ρ sin φ Δθ) rather than raw angle measures

demo_steps.title: The spherical box in place
demo_steps.narration: The orange box sits between spheres ρ and ρ+Δρ, cones φ and φ+Δφ, and planes θ and θ+Δθ. Its projection onto the xy-plane is the blue quadrilateral, whose base edge is ρ sin φ Δθ.

demo_steps.title: Radial increment Δρ
demo_steps.narration: Drag Δρ: the box thickens radially between the two dashed sphere arcs. This edge length equals Δρ exactly — no scaling factor needed.

demo_steps.title: Angular increments are arcs
demo_steps.narration: Drag Δφ and Δθ: those edges stretch as arcs whose lengths are ρΔφ and ρ sin φ Δθ. The azimuth edge shrinks toward the z axis — the origin of the sin φ factor.

demo_steps.title: Magnified element and ΔV
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the enlarged view: the same box is blown up with edges Δρ, ρΔφ, ρ sin φ Δθ highlighted in correspondence with the in-place box. Multiplying gives ΔV = ρ² sin φ Δρ Δφ Δθ.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Axes span ±4 units; box centered at spherical ρ=2.2, φ≈50° from +z, θ≈40° from +x in the first octant. Box edges: radial Δρ (default 0.3 world units), meridian arc ρ·Δφ, azimuth arc ρ·sinφ·Δθ. The box is a curved wedge built between spheres of radius ρ and ρ+Δρ, cones at φ and φ+Δφ, half-planes at θ and θ+Δθ — build it from a parametric surface patch or a BoxGeometry bent to follow the arcs. Dashed arcs at radius ρ and ρ+Δρ in the meridian plane sweep from the z axis down through the box; dashed rays from the origin fan to the box's corners. Δρ bracket sits on the z axis between heights where the two sphere radii cross it. Blue projection quad in the z=0 plane directly beneath the box (#4472c4, ~0.85 opacity). Gray curved arrow (#b0b0b0, thick tube) arcs from near the box up and right toward the inset region. Inset box: an enlarged straight-edged parallelepiped copy of the wedge (edges Δρ × ρΔφ × ρ sinφ Δθ, scaled up ~2×) placed to the right of the coordinate diagram, orange with lighter top face. The edge currently driven by a slider is highlighted (bright outline #cc3300) simultaneously on the in-place box and the inset box. Colors: axes black, box orange gradient #f4a460 to #e07b39 with lighter top #f9d9b8, dashed construction lines gray #888888, labels black.
interactionPlan.notes: Rebuild the wedge parametrically from (ρ, φ, θ, Δρ, Δφ, Δθ) on every slider change so the curved edges stay correct; the inset parallelepiped's three edge lengths are derived from the same parameters. Keep the dashed arcs, rays, and the blue projection quad recomputed from the same state. The gray arrow is static decoration. Highlight the active edge in both locations by drawing an emissive outline tube along that edge. Labels can be HTML sprites positioned at edge midpoints; the labelView toggle swaps which label set (in-place vs enlarged) is emphasized and which box the camera subtly favors.

authoredContext:
Now we can illustrate the following theorem for triple integrals in spherical coordinates with (ρijk*,θijk*,φijk*) being any sample point in the spherical subbox Bijk. For the volume element of the subbox ΔV in spherical coordinates, we have ΔV=(Δρ)(ρΔφ)(ρsinφΔθ),, as shown in the following figure.

The volume element of a box in spherical coordinates.

In the spherical coordinate space, a box is projected onto the polar coordinate plane. On the polar coordinate plane, the projection has area rho sin phi Delta theta. On the z axis, a distance Delta rho is indicated, and from these boundaries, angles are made that project through the edges of the box. There is also a blown up version of the box that shows it has sides Delta rho, rho Delta phi, and rho sin phi Delta theta, with overall volume Delta V = rho squared sin phi Delta rho Delta phi Delta theta.

As with the other multiple integrals we have examined, all the properties work similarly for a triple integral in the spherical coordinate system, and so do the iterated integrals. Fubini’s theorem takes the following form.

plan.contextChunk: This figure pairs a coordinate diagram with a magnified inset to define the volume element in spherical coordinates. On the left, x, y, and z axes radiate from a common origin and a small curved orange box floats above the first octant, bounded by two dashed circular arcs of slightly different radii and by dashed rays fanning out from the origin. A bracket on the z axis marks the radial increment Delta rho, the angular gap between the two rays reaching the box is marked Delta phi, and a small angle in the horizontal plane near the origin is marked Delta theta. A flat blue quadrilateral in the xy-plane is the projection of the box, with a bracket beneath labeled rho sin phi and an arrow into it labeled rho sin phi Delta theta. A thick gray curved arrow sweeps right to an enlarged copy of the same box, whose three edges are labeled Delta rho, rho Delta phi, and rho sin phi Delta theta, with Delta V = rho^2 sin phi Delta rho Delta phi Delta theta printed below. Showing the subbox in place and again blown up lets each edge be matched to the coordinate increment that generates it. The construction motivates the factor rho^2 sin phi that appears when a triple integral is rewritten in spherical coordinates.

interactions.label: Δρ (radial increment)
interactions.teaches: Stretching the radial increment thickens the box between the two spheres — this edge's length is the raw increment Δρ itself, with no scaling factor

interactions.label: Δφ (polar angle increment)
interactions.teaches: Widening the polar angle gap stretches the box along the meridian arc — the edge length is the arc ρΔφ, which grows with distance ρ from the origin, not the raw angle

interactions.label: Δθ (azimuth increment)
interactions.teaches: Widening the azimuth gap stretches the box along the latitude circle — the edge length is ρ sin φ Δθ, shrinking toward the z axis, which is exactly where the sin φ factor in ΔV comes from

interactions.label: Edge labels
interactions.teaches: Matching each edge of the small in-place box to its blown-up labeled counterpart shows why two of the three edges are arc lengths (ρΔφ, ρ sin φ Δθ) rather than raw angle measures

demo_steps.title: The spherical box in place
demo_steps.narration: The orange box sits between spheres ρ and ρ+Δρ, cones φ and φ+Δφ, and planes θ and θ+Δθ. Its projection onto the xy-plane is the blue quadrilateral, whose base edge is ρ sin φ Δθ.

demo_steps.title: Radial increment Δρ
demo_steps.narration: Drag Δρ: the box thickens radially between the two dashed sphere arcs. This edge length equals Δρ exactly — no scaling factor needed.

demo_steps.title: Angular increments are arcs
demo_steps.narration: Drag Δφ and Δθ: those edges stretch as arcs whose lengths are ρΔφ and ρ sin φ Δθ. The azimuth edge shrinks toward the z axis — the origin of the sin φ factor.

demo_steps.title: Magnified element and ΔV
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the enlarged view: the same box is blown up with edges Δρ, ρΔφ, ρ sin φ Δθ highlighted in correspondence with the in-place box. Multiplying gives ΔV = ρ² sin φ Δρ Δφ Δθ.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Axes span ±4 units; box centered at spherical ρ=2.2, φ≈50° from +z, θ≈40° from +x in the first octant. Box edges: radial Δρ (default 0.3 world units), meridian arc ρ·Δφ, azimuth arc ρ·sinφ·Δθ. The box is a curved wedge built between spheres of radius ρ and ρ+Δρ, cones at φ and φ+Δφ, half-planes at θ and θ+Δθ — build it from a parametric surface patch or a BoxGeometry bent to follow the arcs. Dashed arcs at radius ρ and ρ+Δρ in the meridian plane sweep from the z axis down through the box; dashed rays from the origin fan to the box's corners. Δρ bracket sits on the z axis between heights where the two sphere radii cross it. Blue projection quad in the z=0 plane directly beneath the box (#4472c4, ~0.85 opacity). Gray curved arrow (#b0b0b0, thick tube) arcs from near the box up and right toward the inset region. Inset box: an enlarged straight-edged parallelepiped copy of the wedge (edges Δρ × ρΔφ × ρ sinφ Δθ, scaled up ~2×) placed to the right of the coordinate diagram, orange with lighter top face. The edge currently driven by a slider is highlighted (bright outline #cc3300) simultaneously on the in-place box and the inset box. Colors: axes black, box orange gradient #f4a460 to #e07b39 with lighter top #f9d9b8, dashed construction lines gray #888888, labels black.
interactionPlan.notes: Rebuild the wedge parametrically from (ρ, φ, θ, Δρ, Δφ, Δθ) on every slider change so the curved edges stay correct; the inset parallelepiped's three edge lengths are derived from the same parameters. Keep the dashed arcs, rays, and the blue projection quad recomputed from the same state. The gray arrow is static decoration. Highlight the active edge in both locations by drawing an emissive outline tube along that edge. Labels can be HTML sprites positioned at edge midpoints; the labelView toggle swaps which label set (in-place vs enlarged) is emphasized and which box the camera subtly favors.
